required_behavior: Executable-reference discovery gives a well-formed, terminated, quoted non-shell interpreter heredoc body a syntax-aware view so that data read by that body cannot be promoted to a shell script candidate, while the original source text still feeds direct lifecycle detection and real referenced shell scripts remain blocked; malformed, unquoted, unknown-consumer and compound forms keep the conservative walk.

evidence.reference: same TS-389 canary run against an extracted tree at upstream 4f22543509d1b91dc45bcb369447126c5eb14fb7
evidence.result: The inspected upstream revision reproduces the defect: the harmless quoted-Python heredoc log read is still blocked, while the direct restart and referenced real script are correctly blocked and the python3 -c equivalent is allowed.

Upstream masks inert heredoc bodies only for the direct lifecycle scan; referenced-script discovery still receives the raw command, so a path inside a quoted interpreter heredoc body is still promoted to a script candidate.

retirement_gate.summary: Retire only when an adopted exact Hermes release provides a syntax-aware referenced-script walk that accepts inert interpreter heredoc data while still blocking direct lifecycle commands and referenced real scripts, verified against the recorded control matrix.
